headline: Gold price today: Spot gold hits one-week low, slips to $4,100 per ounce
body: Gold prices remained under pressure as investors assessed a mix of global and domestic cues, including movements in the US dollar, Treasury yields, c
full_body:
Gold prices extended their losses, falling to their lowest level in nearly a week as a stronger US dollar and higher crude oil prices dampened investor appetite for the safe-haven metal. Spot gold eased 0.1% to $4,100.32 per ounce by 0107 GMT after touching its weakest level since July 2 earlier in the session, while US gold futures for August delivery dropped 1.1% to $4,112.50 per ounce.

The decline came after US strikes on Iran lifted oil prices, fuelling concerns that inflationary pressures could persist. Higher inflation expectations have raised fears that the US Federal Reserve may keep interest rates elevated for longer, reducing the appeal of non-yielding assets such as gold. As a result, investors remained cautious, with bullion coming under pressure despite lingering geopolitical uncertainty.

International gold prices also came under pressure, with spot gold falling nearly 0.6% while silver slipped around 2%. Analysts linked the decline to a rebound in crude oil prices following attacks on shipping routes around the Strait of Hormuz. Rising crude prices fuelled concerns over inflation and lifted both US Treasury yields and the dollar index.

Since gold is priced in dollars, a stronger greenback makes the metal more expensive for overseas buyers, reducing demand. Higher bond yields further diminished gold's attractiveness because investors could earn better returns from fixed-income assets. These combined factors created fresh pressure on international bullion markets.

Market participants largely stayed on the sidelines as they awaited several important economic events from the United States. The release of the Federal Reserve's June meeting minutes, the second round of US-Iran peace talks, ADP employment data, jobless claims and inflation figures were expected to provide fresh direction to gold prices.

Investors typically prefer to avoid aggressive positions before such high-impact events because monetary policy expectations directly influence bullion demand. Since gold does not offer interest income, expectations of higher interest rates generally reduce its appeal. Analysts therefore noted that traders adopted a cautious approach, contributing to the weakness in bullion prices as markets waited for greater clarity from upcoming economic data.

Gold prices have recorded a steep decline in the domestic market, with the price of 99.9% purity gold falling by Rs 1,400 to Rs 1,49,250 per 10 grams from the previous session. Silver also moved lower, shedding Rs 200 to Rs 2,39,800 per kilogram on Tuesday. Analysts attributed the decline to a combination of a stronger rupee and weakness in global bullion markets. A stronger domestic currency makes imported gold cheaper, thereby reducing local bullion prices.

The fall also reflected cautious investor sentiment ahead of key global events that were expected to influence precious metal prices. The decline in both gold and silver highlighted how currency movements can significantly impact domestic bullion even when international fundamentals remain mixed.

headline: Why are there concerns over WhatsApp usernames? | Explained
body: What is the username feature that WhatsApp intends to roll out? How does it work and what privacy safeguards are built into it? Why is the Indian government asking WhatsApp to stop its roll-out? Can the government dictate an app’s features?
full_body:

Today's Cache Your download of the top 5 technology stories of the day.

O n July 1, 2026, the Union government sent a notice to Meta asking it to stop the rollout of WhatsApp’s username feature, for which the Meta-owned messaging platform is currently taking reservations. In a notice to the social media platform, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) wrote that hiding phone numbers and only showing usernames may increase the incidence of online fraud, phishing, digital arrest scams and impersonation attacks.

WhatsApp advertises usernames as a way to chat without sharing phone numbers. Instead of a mobile number, new contacts will only see your chosen username. This is an optional feature.

There is no search directory of usernames within WhatsApp. To contact someone, you need to know the person’s exact username. For those who are concerned that someone could guess their username, WhatsApp has said they would be able to set a personal identification number (PIN). In that case, even someone who knows your username will not be able to contact you if they don’t know your PIN.

The feature is yet to be rolled out. Meta has said it will be made widely available over the next few months with multiple safeguards in place.

MeitY said in its notice, a copy of which was reviewed by The Hindu, that the feature could “facilitate impersonation and identity spoofing, including impersonation of individuals, public authorities, financial institutions, and government agencies, by permitting the adoption of usernames closely resembling those of genuine persons or institutions”.

Echoing MeitY’s concerns, some public personalities have said that variations of their names have already been reserved by users. In a post on X, MobiKwik founder Bipin Preet Singh said this had happened to him. He wrote: “Not a good idea at all. Will lead to proliferation of fraud and impersonation.”
